claims.claim: He was born around 339/340 in Caesarea of Cappadocia and died between 394 and 403.
The work is addressed to a man named Seleucus, who had asked Amphilochius which books should be regarded as divinely inspired.

In the verses Amphilochius gives a systematic list of Old and New Testament books, explicitly excluding several deuterocanonical works and the Revelation of John, thereby entering the contemporary debate over the biblical canon.
The poem was written as a didactic response to Seleucus’s inquiry, combining moral exhortation with a catalogue of the accepted Scriptures.

The text survives only in a few Greek manuscripts that were transmitted together with the writings of Gregory of Nazianzus and has been published in modern critical editions such as the De Gruyter “Patristische Texte und Studien” volume (2019).
